evals.prompt: I need to implement a proper error hierarchy for my Flutter app. I use Dio for HTTP requests and Firebase for auth. How should I structure the Failure sealed class hierarchy and how does FailureMessageKey work?
evals.expected_output: sealed class Failure hierarchy with no hardcoded String messages, FailureMessageKey enum as the i18n bridge, localizedMessage(context) for UI resolution, ValidationFailure as the only justified literal String exception.

assertions.text: Response uses sealed class Failure hierarchy with final class leaf nodes
Response uses FailureMessageKey enum — Failure carries a key, NOT a hardcoded String message
Response shows localizedMessage(context) as the UI resolution method — never exposes literalMessage directly
Response distinguishes ValidationFailure/BusinessRuleFailure as the only exceptions that carry a literal String

evals.prompt: Show me how to implement a datasource method that fetches a user profile from an API using TaskEither.tryCatch. The method should handle DioException and map it to the correct Failure type using ErrorHandler.
evals.expected_output: TaskEither.tryCatch with ErrorHandler.map as tear-off, DioErrorInterceptor as prerequisite that converts DioException to AppException before ErrorHandler sees it, repository returning Either<Failure,T> with no own throw.

assertions.text: Response uses TaskEither.tryCatch with ErrorHandler.map in the second argument
Response mentions DioErrorInterceptor as the prerequisite that converts DioException to AppException BEFORE ErrorHandler.map runs
Response shows repository calling .run() and returning Either<Failure,T> with no own try-catch or throw

evals.prompt: How do I set up global error handling in Flutter so that unhandled exceptions and Flutter framework errors are always captured? Show me what to add to main().
evals.expected_output: GlobalErrorHandler.initialize() before runApp, FlutterError.onError, PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError, runZonedGuarded wrapper, BlocObserver for BLoC projects, ProviderObserver for Riverpod.

assertions.text: Response registers FlutterError.onError for framework errors
Response registers PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError for platform/async errors
Response uses a GlobalErrorHandler class with initialize() called before runApp — not just standalone functions
Response includes BlocObserver (for BLoC) and/or ProviderObserver (for Riverpod) as additional error capture layers
